title: Same Sentence. Different Tokenizers. Different Tokens.

data.kicker: LLM basics cheat sheet · 6 tokenization methods
title: Same Sentence.
Different Tokenizers.
Different Tokens.

intro.before: An LLM never sees raw text, only token IDs. The tokenizer decides
intro.highlight: how text is cut into pieces
intro.after: , which sets cost, context length and multilingual quality.

bullets.text: Starts from characters and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair
Frequent words become one token; the number of merges sets the vocab size
Rare words split into known pieces: “lowest” → low + est
Characters never seen in training can still end up as unknown tokens
Runs BPE over UTF-8 bytes, so the base alphabet is 256 and nothing is unknown
Handles any language, emoji and code; GPT-2’s vocab is 50,257 tokens
The standard for GPT-style LLMs (tiktoken, Llama 3)
Non-English text often needs more tokens than English for the same sentence
Picks merges that most raise the training data’s likelihood, not raw counts
Splits words greedily by longest match: unaffable → un ##aff ##able
Powers BERT and its family (BERT-base has 30,522 tokens)
Falls back to [UNK] when a word can’t be split, losing it entirely
Starts with a large vocab and prunes the pieces that matter least
Picks the most probable split: hell + o (0.0010) beats he + llo (0.0004)
Treats spaces as ▁, so it works for languages without spaces (T5, ALBERT)
Slower to train than BPE, and its splits are harder to predict
A tiny vocabulary (about 100 symbols for English) and no rare words
Sees spelling directly, which helps with typos and word games
“tokenization” becomes 12 tokens instead of 2, so sequences get long
Attention grows with length squared: 144 vs 4 pairs, 36× the work
Feeds raw UTF-8 bytes to the model: 256 values plus a few special tokens
No tokenizer to train, version or mismatch between training and serving
Robust to typos, noise and rare scripts, since every byte is known
Byte sequences run several times longer than subwords, so it costs more

principles.sub: Budget in tokens, not words; in English, one token is about ¾ of a word.
The same sentence can take several times more tokens in some scripts.
Always load the tokenizer that ships with the model checkpoint.

rows.q: General LLM for any text or code
Custom vocab for a new domain

quote.big: The model never sees your words, only tokens.
quote.small: Know your tokenizer before you count costs.
